answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonded reputation river: each identity stakes a refundable bond and earns standing only through completed, peer-reviewed work, so a fresh fake cannot buy history. When many accounts emit the same signal — identical outputs, timing, and a nebula of near-duplicate templates — the registry slashes the bond and revokes the cluster. Creating thousands of credible identities then costs real stake and sustained work, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
